I've written the notes below. A few gaps first, so you know what's missing:

- **Missing traditions.** I didn't find anything on the Lutheran sites (lcms.org, 1517.org) or the Wesleyan sites (wesley.nnu.edu, seedbed.com). The Lutheran view comes only through Luther's own words, quoted on gty.org. I found no Orthodox source, no netbible.org notes, and no prosperity, word-of-faith or hyper-grace teaching on this chapter.
- **Catholic view.** I only found the Catholic reading of v. 15. I couldn't get a Catholic source on the man of lawlessness.
- **Unread pages.** The Ellicott chapter page wouldn't load, so his points come only from search snippets. The Enduring Word page cut off partway through v. 4. Its points on vv. 5–12 also come from snippets, and I have none of its notes on vv. 13–17.

# 2 Thessalonians 2 – Notes

**v. 1:**
- **Coming and gathering.** David Guzik (Enduring Word) says the wording separates "the coming" from "our gathering." He takes this as two stages of Christ's return: one *for* the church (the rapture) and one *with* the church to judge the world. He also quotes Morris, who calls them two parts of one great event. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-thessalonians-2/
- **A Protestant split (rapture).** In an article by George Ladd, the Bible teacher Erdman is quoted saying that the idea of a secret rapture that could happen at any moment, before the Tribulation, "appears to be founded upon a false interpretation of the translation, in the King James Version of the opening verse" of this chapter. https://www.monergism.com/historic-hope-church-0

**v. 2:**
- **"Has already come."** Guzik says the verb means "is present," not "is near." The Thessalonians feared they were already in the Day of the Lord, not that it was coming soon. He thinks the false message may have come through a mistaken prophecy or a forged letter. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-thessalonians-2/
- **Forged letter.** Whedon's Commentary says the word "as" points to some letter falsely rumoured as from him, not to Paul's first letter. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/whe/2-thessalonians-2.html

**v. 3:**
- **Paul's main point.** Christ's return has not happened yet because certain things must come first: the "rebellion" must "come first," and "the man of lawlessness" must be revealed. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/what-2-thessalonians-2-means/
- **"The rebellion."** Guzik says it may mean believers falling away, a worldwide revolt, or both. He rejects the idea that the word means the church's "departure" in the rapture. The word implies something sinful, and the church doesn't leave by its own choice. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-thessalonians-2/
- **A falling away inside the church.** Ellicott thinks the man of sin will have been part of the Christian church at some point (or will still claim to be), and that the rebellion comes to a head in him. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/2-thessalonians-2.html
- **A religious revolt.** Whedon says it is not a political rebellion or revolt; it is a religious turning away from Christ. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/whe/2-thessalonians-2.html
- **"Son of destruction."** Guzik says the phrase basically means "the doomed one." https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-thessalonians-2/
- **Clarke** links the phrase to Judas in John 17:12. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/acc/2-thessalonians-2.html
- **Who has he been taken to be?** Suggestions listed on Bible Hub include Caligula, Titus, Simon Magus, Nero, the Pope, Luther and Mahomet. The same page says most Protestant commentators have taken him to be the papacy. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/2_thessalonians/2-3.htm
- **A first-century reading.** Ligonier notes that some read the rebellion as the Jewish revolt against Rome. On that view almost any Roman emperor who claimed to be divine could fit. Ligonier also warns against spending too much effort naming the man. https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/the-restrainer

**v. 4 (a major Protestant split):**
- **Reformed and Lutheran: the papacy.** Luther wrote that the papacy is the seat of the true and real Antichrist. The Westminster Confession calls the Pope "that man of sin." https://www.gty.org/blogs/B200214/the-illegitimacy-of-the-pope
- **Calvin** said Paul meant a kingdom, not one individual. He saw it fulfilled in "popery." https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-thessalonians-2/
- **Matthew Henry** says that even if it isn't certain the papacy is meant, the description fits it closely. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/2Th/2Th_002.cfm
- **Charles Hodge** calls the papal reading the common Protestant opinion. https://www.monergism.com/antichrist
- **Older commentators on the same line.** Clarke and Whedon take "the temple of God" to mean the church and the man of sin to mean the papal office (Whedon is often taken to be Methodist, but the page doesn't say so). https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/acc/2-thessalonians-2.html ; https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/whe/2-thessalonians-2.html
- **Futurist evangelicals (Guzik, Got Questions, John Piper): one future person.** Guzik thinks calling the Pope the Antichrist is too simple. He reads the verse as a literal temple in Jerusalem, citing Irenaeus. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-thessalonians-2/
- **Got Questions** links the verse to breaking a covenant with Israel and to the "abomination of desolation." https://www.gotquestions.org/man-of-lawlessness.html
- **Piper (Desiring God)** reads it as the final Antichrist claiming to be God. Only God is above all law, and that is the claim this man makes for himself. https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/the-second-coming-not-before-the-man-of-lawlessness
- **TGC: active inside the church.** The Gospel Coalition article says that since he works in "the temple of God," today's lawlessness is probably at work within the church too. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/what-2-thessalonians-2-means/
- **Ellicott: not atheism.** The man doesn't deny God. He claims to *be* the true God. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/2-thessalonians-2.html
- **Jamieson, Fausset & Brown** see Daniel 11:36–37 behind the verse, with Antiochus Epiphanes as an Old Testament preview. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/2Th/2Th_002.cfm

**v. 5:**
- **"Do you not remember?"** Piper notes that in his short visit (Acts 17), Paul had already taught them a lot about the end times. Here he gently reminds them they seem to have forgotten. https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/the-second-coming-not-before-the-man-of-lawlessness
- **Paul wasn't mistaken.** Jamieson, Fausset & Brown say the verse answers those who claim Paul wrongly expected Christ to come right away. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/2Th/2Th_002.cfm

**vv. 6–7 (the "restrainer"; views really differ):**
- **"What" and "he."** Paul uses both "what" and "he," so the restrainer could be a thing or a person. TGC suggests something within the church: the gospel, ministers of the Word, church government, or the Spirit. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/what-2-thessalonians-2-means/
- **The Holy Spirit and the rapture.** Guzik says the restrainer is the Holy Spirit, who will be "taken out of the way." https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-thessalonians-2/
- **Bible.org (Keathley)** ties the Spirit's removal to the rapture of the church. https://bible.org/seriespage/correction-concerning-day-lord%E2%80%94part-2-2-thes-26-8
- **Bible Hub's study notes** take the same pre-tribulation view. https://biblehub.com/2_thessalonians/2-7.htm
- **Constable** says this identification "implies a pretribulational rapture." He also notes Gundry's different take on the Spirit's role. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/2-thessalonians/2-7.html
- **Government or the Roman Empire.** Jamieson, Fausset & Brown point to the steadying influence of governments. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/2Th/2Th_002.cfm
- **Benson** points to the emperors and magistrates. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/rbc/2-thessalonians-2.html
- **Barclay** thinks the Roman Empire is the most likely answer. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/13-5.html
- **Hodge** says the restrainer is usually taken to be the Roman power. https://www.monergism.com/antichrist
- **Other suggestions.** Ligonier mentions a military or political power that will fall. https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/the-restrainer
- **Utley (Bible.org)** lists the Roman emperor and angelic powers among the options. https://bible.org/seriespage/2-thessalonians-2
- **Who holds which view.** A Bible Hub article says Reformation Protestants often saw the civil ruler, dispensationalists favour the Spirit working through the church, and covenant interpreters lean toward government or the archangel Michael. https://biblehub.com/q/Why_debate_the_restrainer_s_identity.htm
- **Where most agree.** Whoever the restrainer is, it shows God is in charge of the timing. https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/the-restrainer
- **"The mystery of lawlessness."** Guzik says the man of sin brings no new evil, just a stronger form of evil already present. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-thessalonians-2/

**v. 8:**
- **Jesus defeats him.** Guzik says the man of sin can't have come yet, because his career ends with Jesus destroying him. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-thessalonians-2/
- **Historicist reading.** Benson, citing others, takes "the breath of His mouth" as the preaching of true doctrine, which gradually wears down the man of sin. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/rbc/2-thessalonians-2.html
- **Whedon** sees a double destruction. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/whe/2-thessalonians-2.html
- **Coffman** says the man of sin is worn down over time, while the final lawless one is defeated instantly at Christ's coming. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/2-thessalonians/2-8.html

**vv. 9–10:**
- **Satan's copy of Christ.** Guzik shows the parallels: both have a "coming," a "revealing" and miracles. The man of sin is Satan's imitation of the true Messiah. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-thessalonians-2/
- **Real signs, used for lies.** Piper says "false signs" does not mean the signs don't really happen. They happen, but they serve a lie. https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/the-second-coming-not-before-the-man-of-lawlessness
- **Pretended miracles.** Matthew Henry, by contrast, takes them as pretended miracles that propped up the papal kingdom. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/2Th/2Th_002.cfm
- **"The love of the truth."** Piper says the root problem is not an intellectual mistake. People refuse to cherish the truth and find pleasure in unrighteousness instead. https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/the-second-coming-not-before-the-man-of-lawlessness

**vv. 11–12:**
- **God's judgment.** Guzik says the deception only takes root in those who refuse to love the truth. God's "powerful delusion" is a judgment that gives them the lie they wanted. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-thessalonians-2/
- **Pleasure in wickedness.** Piper links v. 12 back to v. 10. The opposite of believing the truth is taking pleasure in wickedness. https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/the-second-coming-not-before-the-man-of-lawlessness
- **Ellicott** says the man of sin's signs, which can't endanger those who love the truth, will be full of tricks for those who never cared about it. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/2-thessalonians-2.html

**v. 13 (election; Protestant views differ):**
- **Reformed reading: chosen from eternity.** Calvin says salvation rests on God's eternal choice, so it can't be overturned. The signs that we are chosen are being made holy by the Spirit and believing the gospel. https://ccel.org/ccel/calvin/comment3/comm_vol42/htm/vii.iv.iv.htm
- **Monergism** argues that faith is the *result* of God's choice, not its cause. https://www.monergism.com/god-hath-beginning-chosen-you-unto-salvation-2-thessalonians-213
- **Matthew Henry:** "We are not the elected of God because we were holy, but that we might be holy." https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/2Th/2Th_002.cfm
- **Spurgeon (Baptist)** calls election eternal, absolute and personal. He warns that it is a choice *to* holiness and faith, and that no one should assume they are chosen apart from holiness. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/2-thessalonians/2-13.html
- **Gill and Barnes** also take "from the beginning" to mean from eternity. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/2_thessalonians/2-13.htm
- **A non-Calvinist reading.** Coffman says God chose all people to be saved, but human free will cancels that in many cases. God's choosing also implies the believer has accepted. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/2-thessalonians/2-13.html
- **"From the beginning" as a point in time.** One commentary quoted on Bible Hub (unnamed on the page) takes it to mean when the gospel first reached Thessalonica. It says salvation rests on God's choice but also involves human conditions. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/2_thessalonians/2-13.htm
- **Manuscript difference.** Some manuscripts read "as firstfruits" instead of "from the beginning." That would mean they were among the first converts in their region. https://bible.org/seriespage/lesson-5-standing-firm-trials-2-thessalonians-213-17

**v. 14:**
- **Chosen for glory.** Steven Cole (Bible.org) says believers are so united with Christ that they will share His glory when He appears. https://bible.org/seriespage/lesson-5-standing-firm-trials-2-thessalonians-213-17
- **John MacArthur** says believers are not chosen for a partial salvation that could be lost, but for glory. https://www.gty.org/library/sermons-library/81-49/election-christs-honor-and-our-blessing

**v. 15 (Catholic and Protestant views differ):**
- **Catholic reading.** Catholic Answers points to this verse to support Sacred Tradition alongside Scripture. On its view, how the teaching was passed on, spoken or written, makes no difference. https://www.catholic.com/magazine/online-edition/the-bible-and-other-traditions
- **Karlo Broussard** argues that the spoken traditions may contain things not in the letters. Otherwise Paul's command would be pointless. https://www.catholic.com/audio/drk/tradition-and-scripture-meeting-the-identity-challenge
- **Protestant reading.** Got Questions says nothing here suggests a lasting body of spoken tradition separate from Scripture. https://www.gotquestions.org/apostolic-tradition.html
- **Grace to You (MacArthur's ministry)** says Paul meant only what the Thessalonians had heard directly from him. https://www.gty.org/articles/A246/Scripture-Tradition-and-Rome-Part-3
- **Pulpit Commentary (Croskery)** argues the traditions were handed straight to the Thessalonians, not passed on to future ages. https://biblehub.com/sermons/2_thessalonians/2-15.htm
- **Steven Cole** adds that "traditions" means what was handed down. For us, he says, that teaching is now found in the New Testament. https://bible.org/seriespage/lesson-5-standing-firm-trials-2-thessalonians-213-17

**vv. 16–17:**
- **Jesus named first.** Cole notes that Paul puts Jesus before the Father here, which honours Him. He says v. 16 looks back to the love God showed when He saved us. https://bible.org/seriespage/lesson-5-standing-firm-trials-2-thessalonians-213-17
- **Why Paul wrote all this.** Piper asks why Paul went into such detail about the rebellion. His answer: Paul wanted to keep the believers at their work and full of good deeds (v. 17). https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/the-second-coming-not-before-the-man-of-lawlessness
- **"Every good word and deed."** Bible Hub notes that this covers speech, service and character. https://biblehub.com/2_thessalonians/2.htm
